rows.author: D007
rows.title_full: AN ACT GRANTING FRANKING PRIVILEGES TO SANGGUNIANG BARANGAYS
rows.abstract: Sangguniang Barangays (SBs are often required to communicate with other agencies. However, the limited budget of SBs also limit their capacity to send communications essential in the performance of their duties. To address this problem, the bill proposes to grans SBs limited franking privileges for communications sent to other government agencies.
rows.status: Scheduled for first meeting/hearing on 2006-08-08

rows.author: D007
rows.title_full: AN ACT PROVIDING ADDITIONAL REQUIREMENTS FOR FILING OF CERTIFICATES OF CANDIDACY, AMENDING FOR THE PURPOSE SEC. 74 OF BATAS PAMBANSA BLG. 881, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE OMNIBUS ELECTION CODE
rows.abstract: An ordinary applying vying for a certain job is required by his prospective employer to present a National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) clearance and a police clearance to determine his integrity, character and trustworthiness. The same should be required of a candidate for public office to show that he has always observed good conduct and has obeyed the laws. This measure seeks to require the presentation of an NBI clearance and police clearance as additional requirements in the filing of certificates of candidacy of persons aspiring to run for public office.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on SUFFRAGE AND ELECTORAL REFORMS since 2004-07-27

rows.mother_status: Business for the day on 2006-03-06
rows.title_full: AN ACT ESTABLISHING THE PHILIPPINE COAST GUARD AS A SEPARATE AND DISTINCT SERVICE ATTACHED TO THE DEPARTMENT OF TRANSPORTATION AND COMMUNICATIONS, FURTHER AMENDING REPUBLIC ACT NO. 5173, AS AMENDED AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.title_short: Philippine Coast Guard Law of 2001
rows.abstract: \"Philippine Coast Guard Law of 2001\". The bill seeks to amend RA 5173 by providing for the establishment of the Philippine Coast Guard (PCG) as a separate and distinct armed service attached to the Department of Transportation and Communications. The PCG, under the bill, shall have its own organizational set-up with uniformed and non-uniformed personnel and shall have the authority to establish Civilian Volunteer Organizations or the PCG Auxiliary which shall assist the PCG in the protection of the marine environment, promotion of safety of life at sea and other activities aimed to enhance maritime community relations.
rows.status: Substituted by HB05304

rows.title_full: AN ACT CHANGING THE NOMENCLATURE OF THE MEMBERS OF THE CUSTODIAL FORCE OF THE BUREAU OF CORRECTIONS AND ADJUSTING THEIR SALARY GRADES ACCORDINGLY AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.title_short: Bureau of Corrections Custodial Force Act of 2004
rows.abstract: \"Bureau of Corrections Custodial Force Act of 2004\". The measure seeks to change the title from \"Prison Guard\" to \"Corrections Officer\" attached to the ranks of the Custodial Force of the Bureau of Corrections and to adjust their salary grades accordingly. Department Circular No. 39, issued by the Secretary of Justice, renamed the Bureau of Prisons to the present Bureau of Corrections to conform to ongoing trends in modern penology - shifting from antiquated punitive system of incarceration to the humanistic rehabilitation approach. The same principle is also applied in the bill.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on JUSTICE since 2004-11-08

rows.title_full: AN ACT CREATING TWO (2) ADDITIONAL BRANCHES OF METROPOLITAN TRIAL COURTS OF THE NATIONAL CAPITAL REGION, INCREASING THE NUMBER OF METROPOLITAN TRIAL COURTS FROM EIGHTY-TWO (82) TO EIGHTY-FOUR (84), AMENDING FOR THE PURPOSE BATAS PAMBANSA BLG. 129, AS AMENDED, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE JUDICIARY REORGANIZATION ACT OF 1980, APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES

rows.author: D007
rows.title_full: AN ACT PROHIBITING THE APPOINTMENT OF ELECTIVE GOVERNMENT OFFICIALS WITHIN ONE YEAR FROM RESIGNATION
rows.abstract: The bill seeks to prohibit the appointment of resigned elective government officials to posts in the government until after the lapse of one year from the resignation of the official concerned. This would deter elective officials from accepting offers to assume another position caused by vacancies or resignations of certain officials.  Elected officials who assume vacancies in other posts in the government, in effect, abandon the mandate of the people who elected them.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on CIVIL SERVICE AND PROFESSIONAL REGULATION since 2004-07-27

rows.author: D007
rows.title_full: AN ACT GRANTING CIVIL SERVICE ELIGIBILITY TO CONTRACTUAL AND CO-TERMINUS GOVERNMENT EMPLOYEES WHO HAVE RENDERED A TOTAL OF FIVE YEARS OF EFFICIENT SERVICE, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: Contractual and co-terminous employees are part of the civil service. However, they can not be given permanent appointment due to lack of appropriate civil service eligibility. HB 207 proposes to grant civil service eligibility to contractual and co-terminous government employees who have rendered a total of five (5) years of efficient service. The proposal would promote efficiency in the service considering that these employees will have the assurance of security of tenure and prevent the frequent turnover of personnel.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on CIVIL SERVICE AND PROFESSIONAL REGULATION since 2004-07-27

rows.author: D007
rows.title_full: AN ACT BROADENING THE SCOPE OF UNLAWFUL PRACTICES OF MATCHING FILIPINO WOMEN FOR MARRIAGE TO FOREIGN NATIONALS TO INCLUDE VARIOUS SCHEMES MADE AVAILABLE THROUGH THE INTERNET, AMENDING FOR THIS PURPOSE REPUBLIC ACT NO. 6955
rows.abstract: RA 6955 declared as unlawful the practice of matching Filipino women for marriage to foreign nationals on a mail-order basis and similar practices.  However, RA 6955 failed to anticipate the evolution of the e-mail bride scheme. The bill aims to broaden the scope of unlawful and punishable schemes of matching Filipino women to foreign nationals to include those made through e-mail and/or websites in the internet.  A number of syndicates use these schemes to recruit women into prostitution.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on WOMEN since 2004-07-27

rows.author: D007
rows.title_full: AN ACT INCREASING THE PENALTY IMPOSED AGAINST POLLUTERS OF NAVIGABLE WATERS BY AMENDING SECTION 7 OF PRESIDENTIAL DECREE NO. 979 PROVIDING FOR THE REVISION OF PRESIDENTIAL DECREE NO. 600 GOVERNING MARINE POLLUTION
rows.abstract: It is imperative that stiff civil and criminal penalties be imposed against polluters of our marine environment since we are dependent on the sea and other bodies of water for our transportation, livelihood and other related activities. The bill seeks to increase the penalties being imposed under the present law to a fine of not less that five million pesos (PhP 5.0) or imprisonment of not less than 8 years and 1 day nor more than 12 years or both such fine and imprisonment.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on REVISION OF LAWS since 2004-07-27

rows.author: D007
rows.title_full: AN ACT GRANTING THE RIGHT TO FRANCHISEES TO DEVELOP THE RURAL AIRPORT INFRASTRUCTURE NETWORK IN THE PHILIPPINES FOR COMMERCIAL AND OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: Our government places the highest priority on poverty alleviation, particularly in the countryside. As a strategy to achieve this, the government should focus on rural development coupled with private sector participation. The establishment of private rural airport infrastructures will encourage economic activity in the hinterlands, by serving not only as transportation hubs, but also as industrial, commercial and service centers which will provide the countryside employment to uplift the standard of living in the rural areas.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on TRANSPORTATION since 2005-01-12

rows.author: D007
rows.title_full: AN ACT PENALIZING THE PROVISION OF FIREARMS, AMMUNITIONS, EXPLOSIVES, CHEMICAL, BIOLOGICAL OR NUCLEAR WEAPONS OR ANY PARTS OR COMPONENTS USED IN THE MANUFACTURE THEREOF TO ENEMIES OF THE STATE
rows.abstract: There has been an upsurge of crimes affecting public order and safety due to the proliferation of illegally possessed and manufactured firearms, ammunition and explosives. The bill renders as unlawful for any person, natural or juridical to knowingly sell, transfer, or in any manner provide, directly or indirectly, firearms, ammunitions, explosives, chemical, biological or nuclear weapons or any part or component used in the manufacture thereof, to enemies of the State. It also proposes a penalty of reclusion perpetua to death and a fine ranging from Php 500,000 to PhP 1.0 million for any violation of the proposed law.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on PUBLIC ORDER AND SAFETY since 2004-07-27

rows.author: D007
rows.mother_status: Business for the day on 2006-08-16
rows.title_full: AN ACT AMENDING ARTICLE 16 OF EXECUTIVE ORDER NO. 209 AS AMENDED BY EXECUTIVE ORDER NO. 227, OTHEWISE KNOWN AS THE FAMILY CODE OF THE PHILIPPINES, MAKING IT MANDATORY FOR COUPLES TO UNDERGO COUNSELING PRIOR TO THE ISSUANCE OF A MARRIAGE LICENSE
rows.title_short: Mandatory Marriage Counseling Act
rows.abstract: \"Mandatory Marriage Counseling Act\". The present law only prescribes marriage counseling in cases where parental consent or parental advise is needed. This bill aims to provide for mandatory counseling for all couples intending to marry. It seeks to educate couples on the rigors of marriage and how to cope with the challenges that will face them everyday for the rest of their lives.
rows.status: Substituted by HB05607

rows.author: D007
rows.title_full: AN ACT ESTABLISHING A MECHANISM FOR THE NATIONAL IDENTIFICATION SYSTEM IN THE PHILIPPINES, PROVIDING FOR BENEFITS AND RIGHTS AND CORRESPONDING OBLIGATIONS, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.title_short: National Identification Card System (NICS) Act of 2001
rows.abstract: \"National Identification Card System (NICS) Act of 2001\". In some countries like Malaysia, Indonesia, Japan, Germany and South Africe, the adoption of an identification system has provided a useful tool in minimizing, if not eradicating, bureaucratic red tape. The bill seeks to establish an identification system in the Philippines with the aim of reaping the same benefits as those achieved in the abovementioned countries - efficient delivery of service and effective law enforcement.
rows.status: Under study by the Technical Working Group(TWG) on 2006-09-13

committee_action.action: Under study by the Technical Working Group(TWG) on 2006-09-13

rows.author: D007
rows.title_full: AN ACT PROVIDING FOR THE REORGANIZATION OF THE NATIONAL POLICE COMMISSION, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.title_short: National Police Commission Act of 2002
rows.abstract: \"National Police Commission Act of 2002\". The bill provides for the reorganization of the National Police Commission to enable it to effectively discharge its functions as described in the Constitution and in pertinent statutes. The Commission shall take charge of police operations relating to the public safety of the nation, administer affairs concerning police education, police commission, criminal identification, criminal statistics and police equipment.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on GOVERNMENT REORGANIZATION since 2004-07-27

rows.author: D007
rows.title_full: AN ACT PRESCRIBING A FIXED TERM FOR THE CHIEF OF STAFF AND MAJOR SERVICE COMMANDERS OF THE ARMED FORCES OF THE PHILIPPINES AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.title_short: Prescribing a Fixed Term for the Chief of Staff and Major Service Commanders of the AFP
rows.abstract: Programs of whatever nature usually require a certain length of time to materialize. The person at the helm should likewise enjoy a length of service or security of tenure, to allow him/her adequate time to plan, test and execute programs. This bill endeavors to shield the selection process for the Chief of Staff and Major Service Commanders of the Armed Forces of the Philippines from political and personal considerations by fixing  their term of office to 3 years and 2 years, respectively. Extension of term shall not be allowed except for the Chief of Staff whose term may be extended in cases of war or national emergency.
rows.status: Senate agreed on Conference Committee Report on 2006-12-06
rows.remarks: A similar SB- SB 1862 was passed by the Senate on Mar.7, 2005.

rows.title_short: Omnibus Housing and Urban Development Act of 2004
rows.abstract: \"Omnibus Housing and Urban Development Act of 2004\". The country is beset by the problem of shelter. While at present there are government agencies tasked to address certain aspects of the shelter program, the government needs to focus its efforts and its limited resources to make it more efficient and effective. The bill seeks the creation of the Department of Housing and Urban Development to rationalize the shelter and urban development program. It is envisioned to streamline the bureaucracy and the process of formulating human settlement programs to meet the demand of our increasing population and decreasing space.

rows.title_full: AN ACT GRANTING THE MAGNA CARTA FOR DAY CARE WORKERS, PROVIDING FUNDS THEREFOR, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.title_short: Magna Carta for Day Care Workers
rows.abstract: \"Magna Carta for Day Care Workers\". A large share in the responsibility of childhood development falls on the shoulders of day care workers. Hence, we consider them \"partners\" of many parents in providing early education to our children. However, they are not given the security of tenure, salary and compensation commensurate to the service they render. The proposed bill seeks to promote, protect  and improve the social and economic welfare of day care workers. It also aims to professionalize the sector that  provides substitute parenting to our children.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on SOCIAL SERVICES since 2004-07-27

rows.author: D007
rows.title_full: AN ACT PROMOTING THE WELFARE OF THE PHILIPPINE COAST GUARD BY INCREASING, INTEGRATING AND RATIONALIZING THE BASE PAY AND OTHER BENEFITS OF ITS OFFICERS AND ENLISTED PERSONNEL, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.title_short: The Magna Carta of the Philippine Caost Guard
rows.abstract: \"The Magna Carta of the Philippine Coast Guard\". The bill seeks to provide additional benefits to members of the Philippine Coast Guard (PCG) who are not covered under RA 9166 in view of its transfer as an attached agency of the Department of Transporation and Communications (DOTC). The PCG's transfer to the DOTC enhances the PCG's unique status as a uniformed commissioned service operating outside the military organization and working under the umbrella of a civilian department thus placing it in a category of its own.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on APPROPRIATIONS since 2004-07-27

rows.author: D007
rows.title_full: AN ACT ESTABLISHING A REWARDS FOR INFORMATION CONCERNING TERRORISM PROGRAM AND APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR
rows.title_short: Rewards for Information Concerning Terrorism Act
rows.abstract: \"Rewards for Information Concerning Terrorism Act\". Terrorism has become a threat not only to the lives of individuals but also to peace and order, liberty, property and general welfare essential for the enjoyment of democracy. This bill seeks to provide a reward system for persons who provide information leading to the arrest or prosecution of terrorists or the prevention of terrorist acts.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on PUBLIC ORDER AND SAFETY since 2004-07-27

rows.author: D007
rows.title_full: AN ACT CREATING THE RANK OF FIRST CHIEF MASTER SERGEANT/FIRST MASTER CHIEF PETTY OFFICER IN THE ENLISTED RANKS OF THE ARMED FORCES OF THE PHILIPPINES (AFP), APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.title_short: Creating the Rank of First Chief Master Sergeant/First Master Chief Petty Officer in the Enlisted Ranks of the AFP
rows.abstract: The Armed Forces of the Philippines (AFP) Sergeant Major is the most important adviser to the Chief of Staff on matters concerning the discipline and morale of the troops. To ensure that his authority and responsibility are distinct, the measure proposes to create the rank of First Chief Master Sergeant/First Master Chief Petty Officer (E-10) for the enlisted personnel with the highest rank in both position and grade to be held by the AFP Command Sergeant Major. The bill will also rationalize the pay grade of both the officers' corps and the enlisted personnel.

rows.title_short: National Transportation Safety Act of 2004
rows.abstract: \"National Transportation Safety Act of 2004\". To advance transportation safety consciousness, the bill proposed the creation of the National Transportation and Safety Board (NTSB), an independent, non-regulatory agency, to undertake thorough and impartial investigation of transporation accidents. It shall be responsible for the analysis, evaluation and prevention of air, highway and marine transportation accidents for the effective promotion of safety and prevention of loss of life and property.

rows.title_full: AN ACT ESTABLISHING A MEDICAL AND HEALTH CARE LIABILITY LAW, PROVIDING PENALTIES THEREFOR AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.title_short: Medical and Health Care Liability Act of 2002
rows.abstract: \"Medical and Health Care Liability Act of 2002\".  While the present system provides three avenues that a claimant of medical malpractice may take - criminal court for penal sanction, civil court for damages and the Professional Regulation Commission to suspend or revoke a license - the system itself contributes to the delay, if not denial of justice for the victim. The bill seeks to provide the environment where patients will be provided with the best medical care they deserve by seeking to punish those who perform their jobs with negligence and incompetence and weeding them out of the profession.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on HEALTH since 2004-07-27

rows.title_full: AN ACT GRANTING THE MAGNA CARTA FOR HOMEOWNERS' ASSOCIATIONS, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.title_short: Magna Carta for Homeowners' Associations
rows.abstract: \"Magna Carta for Homeowners' Associations\". Homeowners' associations aim to improve, in their own little way, the quality of life of Filipino citizens albeit such may be limited to their respective memberships only. The bill seeks to remove the ambiguities concerning the role, rights and powers of homeowners' associations by defining and delimiting the same. It will also define the relationship between members and officers of homeowners' associations, the relationships between homeowners' associations and local government units and the relationships between homeowners' associations and concerned national agencies.
rows.status: Substituted by HB04428

rows.author: D007
rows.title_full: AN ACT TO ORDAIN AND INSTITUTE THE MARITIME CODE OF THE PHILIPPINES
rows.title_short: Maritime Code of the Philippines
rows.abstract: \"Maritime Code of the Philippines\". The bill seeks to update and reform the shipping laws of the Philippines and codify the same into one code. It shall upgrade the laws dealing with registration of ships, maritime liens and ship mortgaged, maritime fraud, accidents at sea and shipowners' liability. It provides for a separate common carrier provision to apply specifically to vessels transporting passengers and goods, domestically or internationally. It updates the marine insurance provisions found in the Insurance Code of 1978. The bill also provides for an alternative dispute settlement in the form of arbitration.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on TRANSPORTATION since 2005-01-12

rows.author: D007
rows.title_full: AN ACT CONSOLIDATING ADMIRALTY AND MARITIME LAWS TO MODERNIZE THE MARITIME INDUSTRY, PROMOTE AND REGULATE MERCHANT MARINE ACTIVITIES, RATIONALIZE THE ORGANIZATION AND FUNCTIONS OF GOVERNMENT AGENCIES RELATED TO ADMIRALTY AND MARITIME MATTERS, AND INSURE THE PROTECTION OF THE MARINE WEALTH IN THE PHILIPPINE TERRITORY
rows.title_short: Maritime Administration Act of 2004
rows.abstract: \"Maritime Administration Act of 2004\". At present, the maritime administration functions of the government are spread over seven (7) departments. This structure has resulted in bureaucratic entanglement, functional overlaps and conflicting maritime laws and regulations. These, in turn, has stymied the private sector's dynamism and virtually hamstrung the maritime industry. The bill seeks to put an end to the fragmentation and overlapping of functions of the different government agencies.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on TRANSPORTATION since 2005-02-14

rows.author: D098

rows.title_full: AN ACT ABOLISHING THE DEATH PENALTY IN THE PHILIPPINES
rows.abstract: The measure seeks to abolish the death penalty and for the penalty to be substituted with reclusion perpetua or life imprisonment. Among the arguments for its abolition are: that the death penalty violates the right to life, that the death penalty is not a deterrent to crime as can be proven by scientific studies and that the death penalty is irrevocable and can be inflicted on the innocent.
rows.status: Substituted by HB04826

rows.author: D019
rows.title_full: AN ACT AMENDING SECTION 110 OF PRESIDENTIAL DECREE NO. 1529 OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE PROPERTY REGISTRATION DECREE AND APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR
rows.abstract: The bill seeks to amend Section 110 of PD 1529 (Property Registration Decree) to relieve property owners of the burdensome and onerous task of resorting to judicial actions for the reconstitution of their Torrens Certificate of Title that were lost or destroyed while in the custody of the Register of Deeds. It identifies the Register of Deeds as the proper party to initiate the filing of petitions for the reconstitution of lost or destroyed owner's certificate of title.

rows.abstract: All contractual and casual employees work under the principle of \"no work no pay\". This scheme may be viewed as unfair considering that they too are burdened by the same problems confronting regular employees such as rising cost of living, basic health care and a decent education for their children. rows.title_full: AN ACT TO ESTABLISH A SOCIALIZED AND LOW-COST HOUSING LOAN RESTRUCTURING PROGRAM, PROVIDING THE MECHANISMS THEREFOR, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.title_short: Socialized and Low-Cost Housing Loan Restructuring Act of 2004
rows.abstract: \"Socialized and Low-Cost Housing Loan Restructuring Act of 2004\".  The bill seeks to establish a mechanism that would provide a low-cost housing loan restructuring program. It provides incentives to those who pay monthly amortizations on time by giving them reasonable discounts on their loan interest. Under the bill, all penalties and surcharges shall be condoned upon approval of the application provided that all accrued interests shall be added to the remaining balance of the principal, the aggregate amount of which shall be considered as the new principal amount.
rows.status: Substituted by HB03835

rows.author: D019
rows.mother_status: Approved by the House on 2006-08-07, transmitted to on 2006-08-14 and received by the Senate on 2006-08-14
rows.title_full: AN ACT STRENGTHENING FURTHER AND BROADENING THE COVERAGE OF THE SPECIAL PROGRAM FOR EMPLOYMENT OF STUDENTS, AMENDING FOR THE PURPOSE CERTAIN PROVISIONS OF REPUBLIC ACT NO. 7323, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: The bill seeks to strengthen the Special Program for Employment of Students (SPES) by allowing students to work not only during summer or Christmas vacations but also for the whole year. It also allows small and medium scale enterprises or entities with more than ten (10) employees to adopt the program. It further penalizes any person or entity who refuses or dishonors the educational vouchers paid by the government with imprisonment of not more than six months to one year and a fine of not less than PhP10,000.00.
rows.status: Consolidated into HB00146

rows.title_full: AN ACT DEFINING THE VISION AND POLICIES OF GOVERNMENT IN THE HOUSING AND URBAN DEVELOPMENT SECTOR, CREATING THE DEPARTMENT OF HOUSING AND URBAN DEVELOPMENT, DEFINING ITS MANDATE, POWERS AND FUNCTIONS, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.title_short: Department of Housing and Urban Development Act of 2004
rows.abstract: \"Department of Housing and Urban Development Act of 2004\". Ten years after the passage of RA 7279 (Urban Development and Housing Act), the lack of decent and affordable housing facilities remains to be one of the most pervasive socio-economic problems of the country. This bill seeks to create the Department of Housing and Urban Development that will be responsible for the management of housing and urban development. It aims to streamline the different housing agencies and corporations thereby integrating all housing and urban development polices, plans and programs within the purview of expediting the delivery of decent, affordable and sustainable housing and urban development plans.
rows.status: Substituted by HB04264

rows.title_short: The Political Party Development Act of 2004
rows.abstract: \"The Political Party Development Act of 2004\". The bill seeks to strengthen the political party system and uphold party loyalty. It also seeks to establish a State Subsidy Fund to be used solely for campaign expenditures, operations and programs of accredited national political parties. It hopes to transform the Philippine political parties from personality-oriented to issue-oriented political organizations to provide our constitutents with a better brand of party politics.

rows.title_full: AN ACT RATIONALIZING THE COMPOSITIONS AND FUNCTIONS OF THE NATIONAL LABOR RELATIONS COMMISSION THEREBY AMENDING ARTICLES 213, 214, 215 AND 216, BOOK V, TITLE II OF THE LABOR CODE, AS AMENDED, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: The National Labor Relations Commission (NLRC) and the labor arbiters play a vital role in the maintenance of industrial peace. The bill seeks to rationalize the composition and functions of the NLRC by granting the Chairman and members of the NLRC almost the same functions and duties as those of the Presiding Justice and Associate Justices of the Court of Appeals, respectively. It also places substantial parity in the structure, functions and duties of labor arbiters with those of Regional Trial Court judges.
rows.status: Substituted by HB05015

rows.title_full: AN ACT PROVIDING FOR THE COMPULSORY REGISTRATION OF HEAVY EQUIPMENT AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.title_short: Heavy Equipment Registration Act of 2004
rows.abstract: \"Heavy Equipment Registration Act of 2004\". The measure provides for the mandatory registration of heavy equipment throughout the country. The need for the compulsory registration of heavy equipment is imperative in order to: a) monitor the availabity of construction equipment vis-a-vis the infrastructure needs of the country; b) generate substantial income the government; and c) prevent misrepresentation by unscrupulous contractors as to the ownership of heavy equipment.

rows.title_short: Enhanced Collateral Value of Farm Lands Act of 2004
rows.abstract: \"Enhanced Collateral Value of Farm Lands Act of 2004\". The bill seeks to provide measures to enhance the acceptability of agricultural lands as security for loans obtained from banks and other financial institutions. In the event that the acceptability of agricultural lands as collateral in loan applications is enhanced, access to rural credit will be upheld and encouraged.

rows.title_full: AN ACT AMENDING SECTION 463, CHAPTER 2, TITLE FOUR, BOOK III OF REPUBLIC ACT NO. 7160, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE LOCAL GOVERNMENT CODE OF 1991 AND APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR
rows.abstract: Many of our forests have been turned into virual savannas due to illegal logging activities. Recent events have also proven that uncontrolled and unregulated cutting of logs is the major cause of flooding. To preserve our precious forest reserves and to avoid flooding, the bill seeks the mandatory, instead of optional,  appointment of the Provincial Environment and Natural Resources Officer (PENRO) who shall ensure that the forest lands in every province are protected from wanton and illegal cutting of logs and that reforestations are undertaken in areas where needed.

rows.title_short: The Revised Public Land Act of the Philippines
rows.abstract: \"The Revised Public Land Act of the Philippines\". The measure  amends the Public Land Act of 1936 to provide for an efficient management and disposition of public lands by intensifying the survey of lands, and hastening the disposition and titling of alienable lands, among others. It also provides for the integration of land surveying activities in order to avoid inconsistent land survey data. It seeks the creation of the Bureau of Land Management which shall be the sole government agency tasked to regulate and conduct all land surveys.

rows.title_full: AN ACT STRENGTHENING THE REGULATORY FUNCTIONS OF THE PHILIPPINE OVERSEAS EMPLOYMENT ADMINISTRATION (POEA) AMENDING FOR THE PURPOSE REPUBLIC ACT NO. 8042, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE 'MIGRANT WORKERS AND OVERSEAS FILIPINOS ACT OF 1995'
rows.abstract: Sections 29 and 30 of RA 8042 (Migrant Workers and Overseas Filipinos Act of 1995) provided for the deregulation of recruitment activities and the eventual phase-out of the regulatory functions of the Philippine Overseas Employment Administration (POEA) over the entertainment industry.  Allowing the entertainment industry to run its own affairs in the deployment of overseas performing artists (OPAs) is tantamount to allowing OPAs to be exploited even more.  This bill aims to put a stop to the exploitation of the OPAs by seeking the repeal of Sections 29 and 30 of said Act and thus give the POEA more teeth in protecting the welfare of OPAs.
rows.status: Substituted by HB05498

rows.mother_status: REPUBLIC ACT (RA09346) enacted on 2006-06-24
rows.title_full: AN ACT PROVIDING FOR THE IMPOSITION OF THE PENALTY OF RECLUSION PERPETUA INSTEAD OF THE DEATH PENALTY IN CASES WHERE THE LAW PRESCRIBES THE DEATH PENALTY, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: The imposition of the death penalty has never been and never will be a deterrent to the commission of crime. Heinous crime continue to increase despite the Death Penalty Law. The bill seeks to abolish the death penalty for the simple reason that the Constitution prohibits the imposition of a cruel and unusual punishment. It also provides for the imposition of reclusion perpetua or life imprisonment, as the case may be, in cases where the law prescribes the imposition of the death penalty.
rows.status: Substituted by HB04826

rows.author: D019
rows.title_full: AN ACT EXEMPTING INDIVIDUALS, COOPERATIVES AND OTHER ENTERPRISES ENGAGED IN THE IMPORTATION OF ALL TYPES OF AGRICULTURE AND FISHERIES INPUTS, EQUIPMENT AND MACHINERY FROM PAYMENT OF TARIFFS AND DUTIES, AMENDING FOR THE PURPOSE REPUBLIC ACT NUMBERED EIGHT THOUSAND FOUR HUNDRED THIRTY-FIVE (RA 8435) OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE 'AGRICULTURE AND FISHERIES MODERNIZATION ACT OF 1997'
rows.abstract: The bill seeks to amend the Agriculture and Fisheries Modernization Act (AFMA) by exempting from the payment of tariffs and duties individuals, cooperatives and other enterprises engaged in the importation of all types of agriculture and fisheries inputs, equipment and machineries. At present, the said law only allows the exemption on condition that the imported agriculture supplies shall be used exclusively by the importing enterprise, i.e. the importers cannot sell these products to small farmers, fishers, cooperatives and other members of the agriculture and fisheries sector. Furthermore, the latter can not import directly because only business enterprises, not individuals, are allowed to import under the AFMA.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on AGRICULTURE, FOOD & FISHERIES since 2004-07-27

rows.author: D019
rows.title_full: AN ACT PROVIDING FOR THE EXEMPTION OF FIXED INCOME EARNERS FROM THE FILING OF INCOME TAX RETURNS, AMENDING FOR THE PURPOSE SECTION 51 (A)(2)(b) OF REPUBLIC ACT NO. 8424, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE 'TAX REFORM ACT OF 1997'
rows.abstract: The issuance of certificates of withholding tax to fixed income earners by their employers already serves as a proof of tax payment hence the filing of income tax returns would serve as an added burden not only to these people but also for the government. This bill proposes to simplify the system of tax collection and administration by exempting fixed income earners from the filing of income tax returns.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on WAYS AND MEANS since 2004-07-27

rows.author: D019
rows.title_full: AN ACT DECLARING THE RIGHTS AND OBLIGATIONS OF PATIENTS AND ESTABLISHING A GRIEVANCE MECHANISM FOR VIOLATIONS THEREOF AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: This bill seeks to stop the common practice of hospitals and health care institutioners in detaining patients because of their failure to fully settle their financial obligations. It provides that patients in emergency cases be given medical attention without any deposit, pledge, mortgage or any form of advance payment for treatment. It also provides the patient the right to be informed of his/her illness in a manner and language understandable to the patient. It gives the legal guardian the right to examine and be given an itemized billing statement.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on HEALTH since 2004-07-27

rows.title_full: AN ACT DECLARING AN ELECTIVE OFFICIAL IPSO FACTO RESIGNED FROM HIS OFFICE UPON THE FILING OF HIS CERTIFICATE OF CANDIDACY
rows.abstract: Section 67 of the Omnibus Election Code provides that an elective official running for a public office other than the one he is currently holding in a permanent capacity, except for the positions of President and Vice President, is considered resigned from office upon filing of his certificate of candidacy. This law has been critized as unfair and unequal in the treatment of candidates. The proposed bill seeks to declare any elective official, whether national or local, running for any public office than the one which he is holding in a permanent capacity as ipso facto resigned from his office upon the filing of the certificate of candidacy.

rows.title_full: AN ACT LIMITING THE PRACTICE OF COSMETIC DERMATOLOGY TO LICENSED AND QUALIFIED PHYSICIANS WITH RESIDENCY TRAINING IN DERMATOLOGY
rows.abstract: A significant number of facial care clinics and salons have sprouted and many of these do not have qualified cosmetic surgeons to perform services like facial restructuring and breast augmentation. There have been reports that the practice has resulted to death or caused facial contusions to patients. To protect and promote the right to health of the people, the bill seeks to limit the practice of cosmetic dermatology to licensed and qualified physicians with residency training in dermatology or plastic surgery.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on CIVIL SERVICE AND PROFESSIONAL REGULATION since 2004-07-27

rows.title_full: AN ACT TO ESTABLISH A SOCIALIZED AND LOW-COST HOUSING LOAN RESTRUCTURING PROGRAM, PROVIDING THE MECHANISMS THEREFOR, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.title_short: Socialized and Low-Cost Housing Loan Restructuring Act of 2004
rows.abstract: \"Socialized and Low-Cost Housing Loan Restructuring Act of 2004\". Only 37,000 out of the delinquent 96,000 borrowers availed of the condonation package offered under the Housing Loan Condonation Act of 1998. However, because of another surge of financial crisis, the borrowers were still unable to compny with the terms and conditions of their restructured loan agreement. To provide relief to these borrowers until such time that our economic conditions improve, the bill seeks to establish a socialized and low-cost housing loan restructuring program for the next three years from the effectivity of the proposed act.
rows.status: Substituted by HB03835

rows.title_full: AN ACT PENALIZING THE APPROPRIATION, ENCROACHMENT, REGISTRATION AND TITLING OF CREEKS, ESTEROS, STREAMS, CANALS, RIVER BANKS AND OTHER PUBLIC WATERWAYS AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: Numerous statutes and rulings have been issued to the effect that canals, esteros, creeks and similar waterways are of public domain and as such, may not be acquired by prescription and therefore not registrable. However, despite these laws, encroachment, titling and/or registration of these waterways are prevalent. The bill seeks to penalize the appropriation, encroachment, titling, registration of creeks, esteros, streams, canals, river banks and other public waterways in order to prevent or curtain these anomalous acts.

rows.title_full: AN ACT AMENDING REPUBLIC ACT NUMBERED EIGHTY FOUR HUNDRED AND TWENTY FOUR, AS AMENDED, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE 'TAX REFORM ACT OF 1997', AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: Despite the efforts of the government to provide free quality education, a great number of our citizens are unable to enroll in tertiary and vocational schools because of financial constraints. To help cushion the heavy monetary requirement of pursuing higher and technical education, this bill proposes to allow as a deduction from gross income a portion of the matriculation fee paid by the taxpayer for a qualified dependent. The savings generated can be used by the taxpayer to defray other necessities such as food, transportation and school supplies.
rows.status: Substituted by HB05296

rows.title_short: National Land Use Code of 2004
rows.abstract: \"National Land Use Code of 2004\".  There is an urgent need for a land use code that will allocate land to various competing uses, preserve prime farm lands specially irrigated fields for agricultural purposes, and ensure community participation in defining local land use. The bill provides that a national land use framework be established to define the indicative priorities for land utilization and allocation. A land use policy administration will also be created to set national land use planning and zoning guidelines and standards.

rows.title_full: AN ACT TO PLACE SAFETY NETS FOR FILIPINO RICE PRODUCERS BY IMPOSING TARIFFS IN LIEU OF QUANTITATIVE RESTRICTIONS ON RICE IMPORTS, DIRECTING TARIFF COLLECTIONS FROM RICE IMPORTS TO PROJECTS AND PROGRAMS THAT ENHANCE RICE PRODUCTIVITY AND INCREASE FARMERS'INCOMES, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.title_short: Rice Safety Net Act of 2004
rows.abstract: \"Rice Safety Net Act of 2004\". The bill seeks to adopt the use of tariffs in lieu of non-tariff import restrictions to protect local rice producers in a direct and transparent manner and at the same time, generate revenue necessary to provide the infrastructures and finance the programs that would improve farmers' productivity. The tarrification of rice will stop the destabilizing burden of NFAs intervention mechanisms on the Philippine budget and, at 90% to 100% tariff rate, generate PhP 1.38 billion annually in additional revenues for the government.

rows.title_full: AN ACT ESTABLISHING A PROVIDENT PERSONAL SAVINGS PLAN KNOWN AS THE PERSONAL EQUITY AND RETIREMENT ACCOUNT
rows.title_short: Personal Equity and Retirement Account (PERA) Act of 2004
rows.abstract: \"Personal Equity and Retirement Account (PERA) Act of 2004\". About 20% of the country's total labor force are not covered by any form of retirement plan. Savings account cannot be depended upon to provide financial security to those not covered by retirement plans. Moreover, retirement or pension plans offered by pre-need companies are too expensive. A savings scheme is needed to encourage Filipinos to save for their retirement years. The bill provides for the establishment of a provident equity retirement account (PERA) which is a form of savings scheme that help improve the country's saving rate. It proposes to make contributions to the PERA 100% deductible from the taxable income of the contributor.
rows.status: Substituted by HB06078

rows.abstract: \"Cable TV Act of 2004\". Ar present, cable TV is classified under the broadcast industry although some sectors claim that it belongs to the telecommunications sector. But cable TV can neither be classified as public utility nor media. The proposed bill tries to resolve this issue by recognizing it as a separate and distinct industry meant to supplement and complement the telecommunications and braodcast sectors. The upgrading of the cable TV industry will allow for alternative modes of communication such as cable internet and cable telephony. These modes of communication will help facilitate exchange and delivery of information in the country.

rows.title_full: AN ACT CREATING THE NATIONAL REVENUE AUTHORITY, PROVIDING FUNDS THEREFOR AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.title_short: National Revenue Authority Act of 2004
rows.abstract: \"National Revenue Authority Act of 2004\". The national government's deficit increased from 1.9% of the gross domestic product in 1998 to 4.6% in 2003. To reduce the deficit without compromising development spending, the government needs to improve tax collection, particularly in the Bureau of Internal Revenue (BIR), which accounts for about 80% of total tax collection. The bill seeks the creation of the National Revenue Authority (NRA) to address the taxpayers' growing dissatisfaction particularly over frontline services, high level of tax evasion/avoidance and increasing perception of corruption in the BIR. The NRA is envisioned to be free from political interference.

rows.abstract: The bill provides punishment for refusal or failure of any telecommunications entity to comply with interconnection regulation after having been required by lawful written order of the National Telecommunications Commission. rows.title_full: AN ACT AMENDING SECTIONS 212 AND 214 OF REPUBLIC ACT 7160, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE LOCAL GOVERNMENT CODE OF 1991
rows.abstract: Real property tax (RPT) accounts for about 36% of the total locally-generated income of local government units. However, based on a Commission on Audit report, only 54% of the total potential tax take are actually collected. To improve collection efficiency on RPT, the bill proposes to transfer the approval of the schedule of fair market values from the local Sanggunian to the Department of Finance upon review and recommendation of a regional technical valuation committee. The power to determine the assessment levels and tax rates shall remain with the local Sanggunian.

rows.title_full: AN ACT PROVIDING MEASURES TO ENHANCE THE ACCEPTABILITY OF AGRICULTURAL LANDS AS SECURITY FOR LOANS OBTAINED FROM LENDERS, BANKS AND OTHER FINANCIAL INSTITUTIONS THEREBY PROMOTING ACCESS TO RURAL CREDIT, PROVIDING MECHANISMS THEREFOR AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.title_short: Enhanced Collateral Value Farm Lands Act of 2004
rows.abstract: \"Enhanced Collateral Value of Farm Lands Act of 2004\". Financial institutions accept only Certificate of Land Titles as collateral for loans. The Certificate of Land Ownership Award (CLOA) given by the Department of Agrarian Reform to amortizing farmers are proof that they are beneficiaries of the Comprehensive Agrarian Reform Program (CARP). However, since CLOAs are not yet Certificates of Land Titles, financial institutions are reluctant to grant loans to beneficiaries of the CARP. The bill seeks to authorize financial institutions to accept CLOAs issued under the CARP as collateral for loans. Granting farmers access to financial institutions will surely promote an increase in agricultural production.

rows.title_short: Billion Trees Act of 2004
rows.abstract: \"Billion Trees Act of 2004\". Of the country's forestland of 15.9 million hectares in the 1950s, only about 6.6 million hectares are left today. Thus, there is an urgent need to rehabilitate and reforest our mountains, especially our watershed areas. The bill aims to target the planting of a billion trees covering about 1.0 million hectares over a period of five years. It proposes to tap the police, local government units, military, upland communities, the private sector, NGOs and civic organizations in the reforestation program.

rows.abstract: \"Pre-Need Plan Code of the Philippines\". The proliferation of pre-need corporations has raised questions on the industry's capability to provide security to its investors and planholders. There is a need to regulate the industry to protect its investors and planholders from fraud. This bill seeks to provide the legislative framework that will govern the pre-need industry, provide the regulatory standards within the industry to level the playing field, strengthen the Insurance Commission's regulatory capabilities to insure that the industry does not become a forum for abuse and provide for the effective protection of planholders.

rows.title_short: NO Smoking and NOn-Use of Cellular Phone While Driving Act of 2004
rows.abstract: \"No Smoking and Non-Use of Cellular Phone While Driving Act of 2004\". A growing number of drivers use their cell phones while driving, not taking into consideration the consequences it will bring not only to them but also to their passengers and to pedestrians. On the other hand, the dangers of smoking to health and safety need not be elaborated on. The bill seeks to prohibit all drivers of private and public motor or non-motor vehicles from smoking or using cellular phones while driving in order to protect and secure the safety of drivers, passengers and pedestrians.

rows.abstract: \"National Tourism Policy Act of 2004\". Our tourism industry has grown over the years at an impressive rate. However, the impressive tourism record should not blind us to the alarming state of degradation to our environment and our cultural traditions.  This measure aims to guide the course and pace of tourism development in the country and to ensure the continuity of tourism programs. It promotes ecotourism as a strategy for low-impact, environmentally sound and community participatory programs that promotes a balance between economic development and environment and natural resource protection.

rows.abstract: Television is the most popular means of communication. Unfortunatley, it denies hearing-impaired individuals the full audio-visual experience to be informed of current happenings in the world. This bill seeks to require all franchise holders, operators of television networks or stations and producers of television programs to broadcast their newscast or new programs, which are national and regional in scope, with subtitles in order to benefit persons with hearing disabilities.

rows.title_full: AN ACT AMENDING CERTAIN PROVISIONS OF REPUBLIC ACT NO. 8435, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS 'AN ACT PRESCRIBING URGENT RELATED MEASURES TO MODERNIZE THE AGRICULTURE AND FISHERIES SECTORS OF THE COUNTRY IN ORDER TO ENHANCE THEIR PROFITABILITY, AND PREPARE SAID SECTORS FOR THE CHALLENGES OF GLOBALIZATION THROUGH AN ADEQUATE, FOCUSED AND RATIONAL DELIVERY OF NECESSARY SUPPORT SERVICES, APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: The enactment of RA 8435 (Agriculture and Fisheries Modernization Act) effectively deprived agro-processors of the importation incentives they used to enjoy under the Investments Priority Program (IPP).  Believing that agro-processors have already been covered under RA 8435, the Board of Investments excluded them from its Investment Incentive Program. The lost incentive resulted in a decline in investments in agro-processing activities.  The bill seeks to grant tariff-free importation incentive to the agricultrual and fisheries sectors.  To level the playing field for local and imported inputs and equipment, purchase of the former shall likewise be given an incentive by way of a tax credit equal to the amount of tariff that should have been paid if it were imported.
